meetingTitle: Raffles Place Flagship & App Promo Launch

card.youAre: You are Wei Ling, Operations Director looking after the shop floor, Auntie Mary, food hygiene, and the budget.
facts: Our 28-seat Raffles Place shop has four 4-seater booths (16 seats) with 12 wall sockets and free guest Wi-Fi, plus six 2-seater tables.
Four freelancers held the 4-seater booths for two hours every morning this week on a single $2.20 drink, costing about $420 a morning in lost breakfast sets.

Auntie Mary (62) is the only floor staff who seats solo diners with hot trays and clears tables. A customer in a suit shouted at her last week when she moved his tissue packet, and she will not police seats or touch customers' belongings.
60% of our morning customers dine solo and cannot carry a hot tray of runny soft-boiled eggs without a table.
A customer from our soft trial was hospitalized yesterday with suspected salmonella from soft-boiled eggs; SFA inspectors arrive tomorrow morning at 9:00 AM.
Our egg sous-vide bath dipped below 60°C for 45 minutes during yesterday's rush; pulling soft-boiled eggs completely wipes out 60% of breakfast set orders ($1,800/morning).

Delivery platforms take a 32% commission on breakfast sets ($3.20 on a $10 set), turning delivery orders net-negative. Using our floor staff for in-house deliveries carries rain surge and traffic accident liability.
Our storeroom has two unopened cartons of pasteurized backup eggs ready to heat to 63°C (22 minutes per batch).
card.responsibility: Make sure our plans work for Auntie Mary and the counter staff without breaking food hygiene or blowing our margin.

card.youAre: You are Arjun, Tech & POS Lead looking after the self-order kiosks, the kitchen docket printer, and store power.
facts: The 15-inch kiosk screen fits 12 drink buttons per page and about 18 characters per line.

The kitchen docket currently prints the same button name the customer sees, so renaming a button changes what the kitchen reads. POS v2.4 can hold a separate kitchen print name, but it has to be configured and tested before the morning rush.
When English names printed on kitchen dockets at Tampines, our 65-year-old kopi uncles slowed down by 15 seconds a cup.
The 12 booth wall sockets and guest Wi-Fi run on a programmable smart relay breaker in the back room. Cutting power also hits paying customers using the sockets.

Raising our GrabFood menu price by 30% ($13 for a toast set) triggers platform price-parity penalties, while our direct web QR link only supports self-pickup because the POS has no rider dispatch integration.
POS changes made tonight still need a short kitchen test before 8am.
card.responsibility: Keep the kiosks, kitchen printer, and store power simple enough to configure and test tonight.

card.youAre: You are Mei, Menu & Store Experience Lead looking after our kopi and kaya toast recipes, the menu, and customer flow.
facts: In yesterday's Raffles Place trial, 19 of 28 first-time kiosk users froze for over 2 minutes at 'Kopi O Kosong', 'Kopi C Siew Dai' or 'Teh Halia', and 72% missed the small corner language toggle.

Soft-boiled eggs require continuous 63°C holding to prevent salmonella enteritidis; heating a fresh pasteurized backup batch takes 22 minutes and cannot be rushed without ruining the runny yolk texture.
60% of our morning crowd dines solo while carrying hot trays of runny soft-boiled eggs.
Corporate CBD towers order 20+ toast sets at once on shared GrabFood group carts; if we de-list from GrabFood, office admins will immediately switch orders to Ya Kun.
Local regulars mocked a rival kopitiam on Reddit when it renamed Kopi O to 'Local Americano'.
card.responsibility: Keep our kopi and kaya toast authentic while making ordering and finding a seat easier.

card.youAre: You are Daniel, Marketing Lead looking after TikTok reviews, store promos, and public goodwill.
facts: A soft-trial diner was hospitalized yesterday with suspected salmonella (hospital lab results take 48 hours); Straits Times journalists arrive at 8:00 AM for our ribbon-cutting, and SFA inspectors arrive at 9:00 AM.
GrabFood and Foodpanda deliver 50% of our peak morning volume; de-listing wipes out $2,400 in morning sales and hands the CBD corporate market to competitors.
Adding a 30% price markup on GrabFood ($13 for a $10 toast set) breaches platform price-parity visibility rules and risks immediate customer backlash.
Google reviews dropped to 3.6 stars during our soft trial because breakfast walk-ins could not find a seat while laptop campers held the 4-seater booths for two hours.
card.responsibility: Protect our launch reputation and corporate CBD accounts without making promises the kitchen or floor staff cannot keep.

card.youAre: You are Sam, General Manager chairing the huddle.
facts: Call on the lead for each topic and let the team hash out the practical catches.
Make sure each topic wraps up with a clear call and someone owning the follow-up.
card.responsibility: Chair the huddle, hear both sides out, and assign a follow-up owner for each topic.

agenda.title: First-timers stalling at the kiosk over Kopi names
agenda.decision: how do we help first-time customers order Kopi confidently without slowing the kitchen or losing our kopitiam identity?

openingViews.view: In yesterday's trial at Raffles Place, first-timers jammed the kiosks because traditional names like 'Kopi O Kosong' confused them, and 72% missed the corner language toggle. 19 of 28 first-timers stalled until the queue backed out into the concourse, and with our opening tomorrow at 8am, we need drink ordering clear without losing our kopitiam roots.

The technical issue is that the kiosk software prints the exact button label straight onto the kitchen docket. Our kopi uncles read 1-second shorthand like 'KO'. If we replace local names with long English explanations, the 12-button screen overflows onto page two and slows kitchen prep by 15 seconds a cup.

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Kiosk ordering freeze: 19 of 28 first-timers stalled at 'Kopi O Kosong' and 72% missed the corner language toggle, backing queues out into the mall concourse.
tradeOffs.question: What does a first-timer actually see at the moment they have to choose a drink?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Kitchen docket bottleneck: Dockets print the exact button label; long English names overflow the 12-button screen and slow kopi uncles by 15s a cup.
tradeOffs.question: How do we keep the kitchen ticket readable without pushing half the menu onto a second page?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Peak rush throughput: Kopi uncles scan 1-second shorthand at morning rush; interpreting new ticket labels creates an immediate kitchen logjam.
tradeOffs.question: Who absorbs the extra time if the kitchen has to interpret new labels?

agenda.title: Morning seat crunch & laptop campers
agenda.decision: how do we free up tables for breakfast diners without turning Auntie Mary into seat police or punishing solo customers?

openingViews.view: Soft trial Google reviews dropped to 3.6 stars because breakfast customers couldn't find a table. Freelancers camp in four of our 4-seater booths for two hours over one $2.20 kopi—locking up 16 of our 28 seats—and Auntie Mary got shouted at yesterday just for asking someone to share a booth. We open at 8am tomorrow and need a clear seating rule so staff aren't left fighting customers.

The reason people hold tables is that 60% of our morning customers are solo diners carrying scalding hot trays of runny eggs and kopi. They physically cannot hold a hot tray in a queue without securing a seat first with tissues. If we enforce a blanket ban on table-holding, we leave genuine solo diners stranded with boiling food and turn Auntie Mary into a bouncer.

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Revenue & seat lockup: 4 booths (16 of 28 seats) held for 2 hours over one $2.20 kopi ($420/morning lost); Auntie Mary got yelled at when moving tissues.
tradeOffs.question: Who enforces any new seating rule if it cannot be Auntie Mary?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Solo diners stranded: 60% of breakfast diners are solo customers carrying scalding egg trays and kopi; a blanket ban leaves them stranded with boiling food.
tradeOffs.question: Where does a solo diner with a hot tray sit while the queue clears?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Smart breaker bluntness: Booth sockets and Wi-Fi run on smart relays, but cutting power hits legitimate diners and risks immediate social media backlash.
tradeOffs.question: Is the answer power, layout or timing, and what evidence will tell us it worked?

agenda.title: SFA food safety inspection & salmonella report
agenda.decision: how do we handle tomorrow's SFA inspection and salmonella report without sparking a media panic or wiping out 60% of our breakfast sets?

openingViews.view: A soft-trial diner was hospitalized yesterday with suspected salmonella, and Straits Times journalists arrive at 8:00 AM before SFA inspects at 9:00 AM. Even though hospital lab results take 48 hours, we should pause soft-boiled eggs for the morning and put out a precautionary supplier batch #402 review notice so the press sees us acting first.

Hold on—our sous-vide holding bath dipped to 58°C for 45 minutes during yesterday's rush, and SFA will swab the tank and check our temperature log at 9:00 AM. If we publicly point at the supplier or pull eggs before lab confirmation, we spark a media panic and kill 60% of breakfast sets when we have unopened pasteurized backup cartons ready to hold at 63°C.

tradeOffs.tradeOff: 8am press vs unconfirmed lab: Straits Times arrives at 8am while hospital lab results take 48h; a precautionary pause shows action but risks sparking a launch panic.
tradeOffs.question: What do we tell the 8am press and customers while the hospital lab test is still pending?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: 58°C bath dip & SFA swab: Holding bath dipped below 60°C for 45m yesterday; SFA swabs at 9am, though unopened pasteurized backup eggs can hold at 63°C.
tradeOffs.question: Do we pull soft-boiled eggs completely, or sanitize the bath and run the pasteurized backup batch at 63°C?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Breakfast revenue vs compliance: Soft-boiled eggs anchor 60% of breakfast sets ($1,800/morning); pulling them guts launch sales, but failing SFA's 9am check shuts us down.
tradeOffs.question: Who logs and verifies our 9am SFA inspection protocol on the kitchen line?

agenda.title: Delivery platform 32% commission squeeze
agenda.decision: how do we protect breakfast margins against 32% delivery commissions without losing 50% of our CBD corporate morning volume?

openingViews.view: GrabFood and Foodpanda just hiked commissions to 32%, so every $10 breakfast set delivered to CBD office towers loses $0.40 after packaging. But platforms drive 50% of our morning revenue—$2,400 a morning—and if we delist or slap a 30% markup on single sets, office regulars will switch straight to Ya Kun.

And we can't just redirect delivery orders to our direct web QR link tonight because our POS has no rider dispatch integration and doesn't batch group delivery dockets for the kitchen. Plus, raising our GrabFood menu price by 30% to $13 triggers platform price-parity penalties that bury our store listing.

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Commission vs CBD volume: Platforms take 32% ($0.40 loss per $10 set), but delisting forfeits $2,400/morning (50% of volume) to Ya Kun.
tradeOffs.question: How do we restructure our delivery menu or order minimums so we stop losing $0.40 per set?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Price-parity & POS rider gap: A 30% GrabFood markup triggers platform ranking penalties, and our direct QR link only supports self-pickup with no rider dispatch.
tradeOffs.question: How do we use our POS or QR ordering without violating platform price-parity or needing rider dispatch?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Floor staff runner risk: Pulling counter or floor staff to hand-deliver CBD office orders during 8am rush leaves the shop short-handed and carries injury liability.
tradeOffs.question: Who handles fulfillment at 8am without pulling our counter staff off the line?

situation: We reopen our refurbished Nanyang Kopi & Toast flagship at Raffles Place tomorrow at 8:00 AM.

glossary.Teh C Siew Dai: hot tea with evaporated milk and less sugar
